title.zh: 忙碌的共享信道：竞争还是无冲突？（复1 · 1）

description.en: Why stations on one channel need rules, what contention and collision-free protocols each waste, how that waste changes with the load, and a full-mark answer.

paras.en: If a LAN is under high load, would it be more efficient to use a contention protocol or a collision-free protocol in the MAC sublayer? Briefly explain your answer.
paras.zh: 如果一个局域网处于高负载，在 MAC 子层使用竞争协议还是无冲突协议效率更高？简要解释你的答案。

text.en: Reading it slowly
text.zh: 慢慢读一遍

items.en: **A LAN** (local area network) is a network inside one building or campus. The classic picture: many computers on one shared cable, or on one Wi-Fi channel. Whatever one of them sends, all the others hear.
items.zh: **局域网**（LAN, local area network）是一栋楼或一个校园里的网络。经典的样子：很多台电脑接在同一根电缆上，或者用同一个 Wi-Fi 信道。其中一台发的东西，其他所有机器都听得到。

items.en: **The MAC sublayer** (medium access control) is the lower part of the data link layer. It has one job: decide who may send next on the shared channel.
items.zh: **MAC 子层**（medium access control，介质访问控制）是数据链路层的下半部分。它只有一项职责：决定共享信道上下一个由谁来发。

items.en: **High load**: many stations have frames waiting to be sent, much of the time. (A *station* is any computer on the channel; a *frame* is one unit of data it sends.)
items.zh: **高负载**（high load）：很多站在很多时候都有帧等着发。（*站* station 是信道上的任何一台电脑；*帧* frame 是它发出的一个数据单位。）

items.en: **Contention protocol** and **collision-free protocol** are the two families of rules the question compares. Both are built from the ground up below.
items.zh: **竞争协议**（contention protocol）和**无冲突协议**（collision-free protocol）是题目要比较的两类规则。下面从头把两者搭起来。

items.en: **More efficient**: the channel's time is the resource. Efficiency is the share of that time spent carrying frames that arrive intact, rather than sitting idle, being lost in collisions, or spent on overhead.
items.zh: **效率更高**：信道的时间就是资源。效率是这些时间里真正在运送完好帧的比例，其余的时间要么空着，要么耗在冲突上，要么花在开销上。

text.en: So the question asks: when many stations want to send, which family of rules wastes less of the channel, and why? You need three ideas: why one channel needs rules at all; what each family does and what it wastes; and how that waste grows or shrinks with the load.
text.zh: 所以题目问的是：很多站都想发的时候，哪一类规则浪费的信道更少？为什么？需要三个想法：一条信道为什么非要规则不可；两类规则各自怎么做、浪费在哪；以及这种浪费怎样随负载增减。

text.en: Picture an office where twenty computers share one cable. A frame on the cable reaches every computer, and the one it is addressed to keeps it. If two computers send at the same moment, their signals add up on the wire and neither frame can be read: a **collision**. Both frames are lost and must be sent again.
text.zh: 想象一间办公室，二十台电脑共用一根电缆。电缆上的一个帧会到达每一台电脑，地址对得上的那台把它收下。如果两台电脑同时发，它们的信号在线上叠在一起，两个帧都没法读了：这就是**冲突**（collision）。两个帧都丢了，都得重发。

text.en: The simplest fix is to divide the channel in advance: each computer gets its own time slot (TDM) or its own frequency band (FDM). That suits a fixed group that sends steadily, like phone calls. But computer traffic is **bursty**: a machine is silent for minutes, then sends a burst. With a fixed division, the slots of silent machines go unused while a busy machine waits for its own small share. So a LAN shares its channel **dynamically**, deciding moment by moment who sends. There are two families of rules for doing that.
text.zh: 最简单的办法是事先把信道切开：每台电脑分到自己的时隙（TDM）或频段（FDM）。这适合一群固定的、持续在发的用户，比如打电话。可电脑的流量是**突发的**（bursty）：一台机器沉默好几分钟，然后突然发一阵。固定切分时，沉默机器的那份空着没人用，忙的机器却只能等自己那一小份。所以局域网**动态地**分享信道，每时每刻决定谁来发。做法分两大类。

title.en: Contention: send when ready, sort out collisions afterwards
title.zh: 竞争：有帧就发，冲突了再说

text.en: **Contention protocols** let a station send as soon as it has a frame, without asking anyone. If its frame collides, it waits a random time and tries again (random, so that the two that collided do not collide again). The family, as the course lists it:
text.zh: **竞争协议**让一个站一有帧就发，不用问任何人。如果帧撞了，就等一段随机的时间再试（随机，是为了让撞过的两个站不要再撞一次）。课上列出的这一家子：

items.en: **ALOHA**: send whenever you have a frame.
**Slotted ALOHA**: time is cut into slots and a frame may start only at the start of a slot, so two frames collide only if they pick the same slot.
items.zh: **时隙 ALOHA**（slotted ALOHA）：时间切成时隙，帧只能在时隙开头开始发，所以只有两个帧挑了同一个时隙才会撞。

items.en: **CSMA** (carrier sense multiple access): listen first, and do not start while someone else is sending.
items.zh: **CSMA**（载波侦听多路访问）：先听，别人在发的时候不开口。

items.en: **CSMA/CD** (with collision detection): also stop the moment a collision is heard, so less time is wasted. Classic Ethernet works this way.
items.zh: **CSMA/CD**（带冲突检测）：一听到冲突就立刻停，少浪费时间。经典以太网就是这么做的。

text.en: **At light load this is ideal.** A station with a frame almost always finds the channel free and sends at once: no waiting, no overhead.
text.zh: **负载轻时，这再理想不过。**有帧的站几乎总能碰上空闲的信道，马上就发：不用等，也没有开销。

text.en: **At high load it falls apart.** Count it for slotted ALOHA. Say that on average $G$ frames are sent per slot, counting the retries. A slot carries a frame only when exactly one station sends in it; when two or more do, the slot is a collision. If stations send independently of each other, the share of slots that carry a frame is
text.zh: **负载一高，它就垮了。**拿时隙 ALOHA 算一算。设平均每个时隙有 $G$ 个帧在发（重发的也算）。只有恰好一个站在某个时隙发，这个时隙才运送了一个帧；两个以上，就是冲突。如果各站彼此独立地发，运送了帧的时隙所占的比例是

text.en: and the rest are collisions or empty. In numbers:
text.zh: 其余的时隙不是冲突就是空着。具体的数：

text.en: Past $G = 1$, the share of useful slots **falls** as the load rises: soon almost every slot is a collision. Worse, every collided frame is sent again, which raises $G$ further: under heavy load a contention protocol feeds its own collisions. (Slotted ALOHA's best is 37%, at $G = 1$; plain ALOHA's best is 18%. Listening first and stopping on a collision make each collision much cheaper, but the trend stays: the more stations are ready, the more often they collide.)
text.zh: $G$ 超过 1 以后，负载越高，有用的时隙反而**越少**：很快几乎每个时隙都是冲突。更糟的是，每个撞掉的帧都要重发，又把 $G$ 推得更高：重负载下，竞争协议是在给自己制造冲突。（时隙 ALOHA 最好也只有 37%，在 $G = 1$ 处；纯 ALOHA 最好只有 18%。先听再发、撞了就停，能让每次冲突便宜得多，但趋势不变：准备发的站越多，撞得越频繁。）

text.en: **Collision-free protocols** decide who sends *before* anyone sends, so frames never collide. The two in the course:
text.zh: **无冲突协议**在任何人发之前就先定好谁来发，所以帧永远不会撞。课上讲了两种：

items.en: **The bit-map protocol**: each round starts with a reservation period of $N$ one-bit slots, one per station. Station $j$ puts a 1 in slot $j$ if it has a frame. Everyone hears the whole bit map, so afterwards every station knows the order, and the ready stations send one after another (the bottom of the figure above).
items.zh: **位图协议**（bit-map protocol）：每一轮先有一个预约期，含 $N$ 个一位的时隙，每个站一个。站 $j$ 有帧要发，就在第 $j$ 个时隙里放一个 1。所有站都听得到整个位图，所以预约期一过，大家都知道顺序，有帧的站依次发（上面那张图的下半部分）。

items.en: **Binary countdown**: stations broadcast their addresses bit by bit, starting from the highest bit; a station that sent a 0 but sees a 1 drops out. The highest address left sends. It costs only $\log_2 N$ bits per frame.
items.zh: **二进制倒计数**（binary countdown）：各站从最高位开始，一位一位地广播自己的地址；发了 0 却看到 1 的站退出。剩下的最高地址的站来发。每帧只花 $\log_2 N$ 位。

text.en: What they waste is **overhead**. The reservation bits are paid every round, whether or not anyone has something to send, and a station with a frame must wait for the reservation period and for its turn, even when the channel is otherwise empty. How much that costs depends on the load, and it is worth counting.
text.zh: 它们浪费在**开销**（overhead）上。不管有没有人要发，每一轮都要付预约位；有帧的站即使碰上空荡荡的信道，也得等预约期过完、等轮到自己。这笔开销有多大取决于负载，值得算一算。

title.en: How efficient the bit-map protocol is
title.zh: 位图协议的效率有多高

say.en: Take $N$ stations, and frames that each last $d$ bit-slots. One round lasts $T$: the $N$ reservation slots plus one frame from each of the $k$ stations that set their bit.
say.zh: 设有 $N$ 个站，每帧占 $d$ 个位时隙。一轮的长度 $T$：$N$ 个预约时隙，加上置了 1 的 $k$ 个站各发一帧。

say.en: The efficiency $\eta$ is the share of the round spent carrying frames.
say.zh: 效率 $\eta$ 是一轮里用来运送帧的时间所占的比例。

say.en: **Light load**: only one station has a frame ($k = 1$), so one frame pays for the whole reservation period.
say.zh: **负载轻**：只有一个站有帧（$k = 1$），一个帧要独自负担整个预约期。

say.en: **High load**: every station has a frame ($k = N$). The $N$ reservation bits are now shared by $N$ frames: one bit per frame.
say.zh: **负载高**：每个站都有帧（$k = N$）。$N$ 个预约位由 $N$ 个帧分摊：每帧一位。

say.en: With 64 stations and frames of 500 bits: at light load, 11% of the channel goes on reservations,
say.zh: 代入 64 个站、每帧 500 位：负载轻时，11% 的信道花在预约上，

outro.en: A collision-free protocol gets *better* as the load rises: its fixed overhead is shared by more frames. A contention protocol gets *worse*: more ready stations, more collisions. That contrast is the whole answer.
outro.zh: 无冲突协议负载越高越*好*：固定的开销由更多的帧分摊。竞争协议负载越高越*差*：准备发的站越多，撞得越多。这个对比就是整道题的答案。

prompt.en: Light load: one frame per round ($k = 1$). Write the efficiency in terms of $d$ and $N$.
prompt.zh: 负载轻：每轮只有一个帧（$k = 1$）。用 $d$ 和 $N$ 写出效率。

The bars show what the channel's time is spent on.

text.en: The course's slide puts it in two lines: under low loads, collision-free methods are less attractive because of their overhead; under higher loads, contention methods are less attractive because of the many collisions. Each becomes inefficient, at opposite ends.
text.zh: 课件用两句话说了这件事：负载低时，无冲突方法因为开销而不划算；负载高时，竞争方法因为冲突太多而不划算。两者都会变得低效，只是在相反的两头。

rows.en: sends at once; collisions are rare
reservations paid for few frames; waits for its turn on an empty channel
rows.zh: 为很少的帧付预约开销；信道空着也得等轮次

rows.en: no collisions; overhead shared by many frames
rows.zh: 没有冲突；开销由很多帧分摊

prompt.en: A collision-free protocol never wastes time on collisions. Why is it not the better choice at every load?
prompt.zh: 无冲突协议从不在冲突上浪费时间。为什么它不是在任何负载下都更好？

label.en: At light load its reservations are paid for few frames, and a station waits for its turn on an empty channel
label.zh: 负载轻时，预约开销只由很少的帧负担，而且信道空着，有帧的站也得等轮次

label.en: Collisions still happen during the reservation period

feedback.en: No: in the bit-map protocol each station has a reservation slot of its own, so even the reservations never collide.
feedback.zh: 不会：位图协议里每个站有自己专属的预约时隙，连预约都不会撞。

label.en: It carries fewer frames than contention at high load
label.zh: 高负载时它运送的帧比竞争协议少

feedback.en: The opposite: at high load it uses almost the whole channel, while contention loses most of it to collisions.
feedback.zh: 正相反：高负载时它几乎用满整条信道，而竞争协议的大部分信道都耗在冲突上。

explain.en: Its cost is fixed per round. Shared by many frames it is almost nothing; paid by one frame it is the main cost, and every sender waits.
explain.zh: 它的开销每轮固定。由很多帧分摊时几乎为零；由一个帧独自负担时就成了主要成本，而且每个发送者都得等。

text.en: The answer is a chain of four links; each becomes a sentence on the paper:
text.zh: 答案是四环相扣的一条链，每一环在卷面上写成一句话：

items.en: **What high load means here**: many stations have frames to send at the same time.
items.zh: **高负载在这里意味着什么**：很多站同时有帧要发。

items.en: **Why contention fails**: stations send when ready, so with many ready they collide often; colliding frames are destroyed and must be sent again, so much of the channel time is wasted, and the retries add yet more load.
items.zh: **竞争协议为什么不行**：各站有帧就发，准备发的站一多就频繁冲突；撞了的帧被毁掉，必须重发，大量信道时间被浪费，重发又进一步加重负载。

items.en: **Why collision-free wins**: stations take turns (by reservation, or by address), so nothing collides, and the fixed overhead is shared by many frames.
items.zh: **无冲突协议为什么更好**：各站轮流发（靠预约或靠地址），什么都不会撞，固定的开销由很多帧分摊。

title.zh: 复习课 (1) 第 1 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: A collision-free protocol is more efficient. Under high load many stations have frames to send at the same time, so a contention protocol (e.g. slotted ALOHA or CSMA) would suffer frequent collisions: the colliding frames are destroyed and must be retransmitted, wasting much of the channel's capacity. A collision-free protocol (e.g. the bit-map protocol) lets each station transmit in turn, so no collisions occur, and its reservation overhead is shared among many frames. (Under low load the reverse holds: a contention protocol can send immediately, while the collision-free overhead dominates.)
paras.zh: 无冲突协议效率更高。高负载时很多站同时有帧要发，竞争协议（如时隙 ALOHA 或 CSMA）会频繁冲突：撞了的帧被毁掉，必须重传，浪费大量信道容量。无冲突协议（如位图协议）让每个站轮流发送，不会发生冲突，而且预约开销由很多帧分摊。（负载低时情况相反：竞争协议可以马上发送，而无冲突协议的开销占了大头。）

text.en: The last sentence is not asked for, but one line that says when the answer flips shows the examiner you understand the trade-off rather than a memorised fact. The marks are in the mechanism: *collisions waste the channel* and *taking turns avoids them*; the bare word *collision-free* earns little on its own.
text.zh: 最后一句题目没问，但用一句话说明答案在什么时候反过来，能让阅卷人看出你懂的是这个取舍，而不是背了一个结论。分在机制上：*冲突浪费信道*、*轮流发避免冲突*；光写一个“无冲突”拿不到多少分。

title.en: Limited contention: the best of both ends
title.zh: 有限竞争：两头的好处都要

text.en: If contention is best at light load and collision-free at high load, can one protocol do both? **Limited contention** protocols try. They let stations contend, but in small groups, so a collision involves few stations and is quickly resolved. The course's example is the **adaptive tree walk**.
text.zh: 既然竞争协议在负载轻时最好、无冲突协议在负载高时最好，能不能有一个协议两头都占？**有限竞争**（limited contention）协议就是这么想的：让各站竞争，但分成小组来争，这样一次冲突只牵涉很少的站，很快就能解决。课上的例子是**自适应树遍历**（adaptive tree walk）。

text.en: Put the stations at the leaves of a binary tree. In the first slot every ready station may send. If exactly one does, it gets through. If they collide, the search goes down the tree, depth first: in the next slot only the stations under node 2 may send, then those under node 4, and so on. Each slot probes one group: a group with exactly one ready station gets its frame through, and a group that collides is split in two.
text.zh: 把各站放在一棵二叉树的叶子上。第一个时隙里，所有准备好的站都可以发。恰好只有一个，它就成功了。撞了，就沿着树往下、深度优先地找：下一个时隙只许节点 2 下面的站发，再下一个只许节点 4 下面的，依此类推。每个时隙探查一个组：组里恰好一个站准备好，它的帧就成功送出；组里撞了，就再一分为二。

text.en: At light load the first slot usually holds one station or none, so it behaves like contention. At high load the search quickly narrows to groups of one, so it behaves like a collision-free protocol. (The course's Example 1: only D and G are ready. Slot 1 collides; slot 2, node 2, holds D alone; slot 3, node 3, holds G alone: three slots.)
text.zh: 负载轻时，第一个时隙里通常只有一个站或没有站，它表现得像竞争协议。负载高时，搜索很快缩到只有一个站的小组，它表现得像无冲突协议。（课上的例 1：只有 D 和 G 准备好。时隙 1 冲突；时隙 2，节点 2 里只有 D；时隙 3，节点 3 里只有 G：一共三个时隙。）

title.en: Listening first, how eagerly, and on the air
title.zh: 先听再发、有多心急，以及无线的情形

text.en: The CSMA variants differ in what a station does when it hears the channel busy:
text.zh: CSMA 的几个变种，区别在于听到信道忙时怎么办：

items.en: **1-persistent**: keep listening, and send the instant the channel goes idle.
items.zh: **1-坚持**（1-persistent）：一直听着，信道一空闲马上发。

items.en: **Non-persistent**: if busy, wait a random time before listening again.
items.zh: **非坚持**（non-persistent）：信道忙就等一段随机时间再去听。

items.en: **p-persistent** (slotted): when idle, send with probability $p$; otherwise wait for the next slot and check again.
items.zh: **p-坚持**（p-persistent，分时隙）：信道空闲时以概率 $p$ 发送，否则等到下一个时隙再看。

text.en: The course's comparison: CSMA beats ALOHA, and **being less persistent is better under high load**. It is the same story as the question. With 1-persistent CSMA, every station that was waiting pounces the instant the channel frees up, so under high load they collide almost every time; waiting a random time spreads them out.
text.zh: 课上的比较：CSMA 比 ALOHA 好，而且**高负载时越不心急越好**。道理和这道题一样。1-坚持 CSMA 下，所有在等的站会在信道空出来的那一刻同时扑上去，高负载时几乎每次都撞；随机等一会儿，就把它们错开了。

text.en: **Collision detection** (CSMA/CD) shortens each collision: a station stops as soon as it hears one, so a collision costs a short contention slot instead of a whole frame. **Switched Ethernet** removes the problem altogether: each cable joins one computer to its own switch port, so there is no shared channel to contend for.
text.zh: **冲突检测**（CSMA/CD）缩短了每次冲突：站一听到冲突就停，一次冲突只损失一个很短的竞争时隙，而不是一整个帧。**交换式以太网**干脆把问题消掉了：每根电缆只把一台电脑接到交换机的一个端口上，没有共享的信道，也就无所谓争抢。

text.en: On the air: you cannot hear every collision
text.zh: 无线上：不是每次冲突都听得到

text.en: On a wireless LAN a station hears only the stations within its range, and what matters is a collision at the *receiver*. Two problems follow:
text.zh: 在无线局域网里，一个站只听得到范围内的站，而要紧的是*接收方*那里有没有冲突。于是有两个问题：

alt.en: Hidden terminals: A, B and C in a row; A and C both send to B but are out of each other's range, and collide at B. Exposed terminals: A, B, C and D in a row; B sends to A and C sends to D; B and C hear each other, yet both transfers can go on at once.
alt.zh: 隐藏终端：A、B、C 排成一行；A 和 C 都在向 B 发，但彼此听不到，于是在 B 处冲突。暴露终端：A、B、C、D 排成一行；B 发给 A，C 发给 D；B 和 C 互相听得到，可两次传输其实可以同时进行。

caption.en: **Hidden terminals**: A and C cannot hear each other, so carrier sense tells neither that the other is sending, and their frames collide at B. **Exposed terminals**: B and C hear each other, so carrier sense holds one of them back, although B → A and C → D would not interfere.
caption.zh: **隐藏终端**：A 和 C 彼此听不到，载波侦听告诉不了谁对方在发，两个帧在 B 处撞上。**暴露终端**：B 和 C 互相听得到，载波侦听会让其中一个闭嘴，可 B → A 和 C → D 其实互不干扰。

text.en: **MACA** solves both by talking about the receiver. The sender first sends a short **RTS** (request to send); the receiver answers with a short **CTS** (clear to send), which carries the length of the coming frame. Every station that hears the CTS is near the receiver, so it stays quiet for that long. A station that hears only the RTS is near the sender but not the receiver, so it may send. The CTS silences hidden terminals; exposed terminals stay free.
text.zh: **MACA** 把注意力放到接收方，两个问题一起解决。发送方先发一个短的 **RTS**（request to send，请求发送）；接收方回一个短的 **CTS**（clear to send，允许发送），里面带着接下来那个帧的长度。凡是听到 CTS 的站都在接收方附近，就在这段时间里保持安静。只听到 RTS 的站在发送方附近、不在接收方附近，照样可以发。CTS 让隐藏终端闭嘴，暴露终端则不受限制。

title.zh: 你来：一个安静的局域网

prompt.en: A LAN connects 40 sensors, each of which sends a short reading a few times an hour. Would a contention protocol or a collision-free protocol be more efficient here? Briefly explain.
prompt.zh: 一个局域网连着 40 个传感器，每个每小时发几条简短的读数。这里用竞争协议还是无冲突协议效率更高？简要解释。

key_points.en: The load is light, so collisions are rare and a sensor can send at once
key_points.zh: 负载很轻，冲突很少，传感器可以马上发

key_points.en: A collision-free protocol would pay its reservation overhead (and the wait for a turn) for very few frames
key_points.zh: 无冲突协议要为很少的帧付预约开销，还要等轮次

model_answer.en: A contention protocol. The load is light, so collisions are rare and a sensor can send its reading as soon as it has one. A collision-free protocol would spend most of the channel on reservations that nobody uses, and make every sensor wait for its turn.
model_answer.zh: 竞争协议。负载很轻，冲突很少，传感器一有读数就能马上发。无冲突协议会把大部分信道花在没人用的预约上，还要让每个传感器等轮次。

explain.en: The same trade-off as the exam question, at the other end of the load: contention costs nothing when collisions are rare, while a collision-free protocol's overhead is fixed per round.
explain.zh: 和考题是同一个取舍，只是在负载的另一头：冲突很少时竞争几乎不花代价，而无冲突协议的开销每轮都是固定的。

title.en: Your turn: both ends at once

prompt.en: Which protocol behaves like a contention protocol at light load and like a collision-free one at high load?
prompt.zh: 哪个协议在负载轻时像竞争协议，在负载高时像无冲突协议？

feedback.en: That is collision-free at every load: it spends $\log_2 N$ bits on the countdown before every frame.
feedback.zh: 它在任何负载下都是无冲突的：每帧之前都要花 $\log_2 N$ 位倒计数。

feedback.en: Contention at every load, and the worst of the CSMA family under high load: every waiting station pounces at once.
feedback.zh: 任何负载下都是竞争，而且高负载时是 CSMA 里最差的：所有等着的站会同时扑上去。

feedback.en: Contention at every load: at high load most of its slots are collisions.
feedback.zh: 任何负载下都是竞争：高负载时大多数时隙是冲突。

explain.en: The adaptive tree walk lets everyone contend in the first slot, which is cheap when few are ready, and splits a colliding group in two at each step, so under heavy load it ends up giving each station a slot of its own.
explain.zh: 自适应树遍历在第一个时隙让大家一起争，准备发的站少时很省；一旦撞了就一步步把组一分为二，所以重负载时最后等于给每个站一个专属的时隙。

title.en: Your turn: slotted ALOHA at G = 2

prompt.en: In slotted ALOHA, $G = 2$ frames are sent per slot on average. What share of the slots carry a frame successfully? (A decimal, such as 0.37.)
prompt.zh: 时隙 ALOHA 里，平均每个时隙发 $G = 2$ 个帧。有多大比例的时隙成功运送了一个帧？（写成小数，比如 0.37。）

explain.en: $S = 2e^{-2} \approx 0.27$: only 27% of the slots are useful, and about 59% are collisions.
explain.zh: $S = 2e^{-2} \approx 0.27$：只有 27% 的时隙有用，约 59% 是冲突。

hints.en: A slot is useful when exactly one frame is sent in it: $S = G e^{-G}$.
hints.zh: 恰好有一个帧在发的时隙才有用：$S = G e^{-G}$。

prompt.en: With MACA, A sends an RTS to B and B answers with a CTS. Station E hears B's CTS but not A's RTS. What should E do?
prompt.zh: 在 MACA 下，A 向 B 发 RTS，B 回了 CTS。站 E 听到了 B 的 CTS，却没听到 A 的 RTS。E 该怎么做？

label.en: Stay quiet until A's frame to B has been sent: E is near the receiver
label.zh: 保持安静，直到 A 发给 B 的帧发完：E 在接收方附近

label.en: Send freely: it cannot hear A, so it cannot disturb A
label.zh: 随便发：它听不到 A，也就干扰不到 A

feedback.en: What matters is the receiver. E reaches B, so its frame would collide with A's at B: E is a hidden terminal.
feedback.zh: 要紧的是接收方。E 的信号能到 B，它的帧会在 B 处和 A 的撞上：E 是隐藏终端。

label.en: Send an RTS of its own at once
label.zh: 马上发一个自己的 RTS

feedback.en: The CTS announced how long B will be receiving; until then anything E sends reaches B and spoils A's frame.
feedback.zh: CTS 已经说明了 B 要接收多久；在这之前 E 发什么都会到 B，毁掉 A 的帧。

explain.en: Hearing the CTS means being near the receiver: stay quiet for the length the CTS announced. Hearing only the RTS means being near the sender only: sending is safe.
explain.zh: 听到 CTS，说明在接收方附近：在 CTS 声明的时长内保持安静。只听到 RTS，说明只在发送方附近：可以放心发。
